sources.citation: Smith, D. E., et al. (2010). The Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter Investigation on the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Mission. Space Science Reviews, 150, 209–241. doi:10.1007/s11214-009-9512-y. Data set: LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, NASA Planetary Data System (use the exact data set citation from the PDS product page).

evidence.method: Visible disk fraction by chord integration in the tangent plane at the disk centre (128 chords), horizon sampled per chord; windows are maximal runs of samples, each standing for one step. Terrain horizon: Ray march along great circles of the reference sphere (ground distance on the sphere, step 120 m, from 240 m), bilinear DEM heights, exact 3D elevation angle above the site's radial horizontal plane (curvature included); truncated where a ray meets missing DEM coverage..
assumptions: Observer eye height 2 m above the surface.
Gravitational light deflection is not modelled (JPL Horizons includes it); measured agreement with Horizons is within 0.002 arcsec.
Eye point 2 m above the DEM surface (1942.16 m above the 1 737 400 m sphere).

limitations: Visible fraction is a fraction of the disk's area: limb darkening is neglected.
Out of scope: earthshine, light scattered from nearby terrain, regional illumination maps.
